googleClientHelp: In the Google Cloud console, create a project (or pick one) and enable this API for it.
Under APIs & Services > Credentials, create an OAuth client ID of type "Desktop app".
Paste its client ID (and secret, if shown) below. Google treats a desktop app's secret as not confidential.
While your Google app is in testing mode only the test users you list can sign in, and its sign-in expires after about 7 days.

entries.name: Google Calendar
entries.tagline: Read your calendars and events, and change them when you allow it
entries.about: Lists your calendars and the events in a date range, searches events, finds free time, and (only at the Read and write level) creates, updates and deletes events. Dara asks before using any tool unless you allow it.

access.label: Read only
access.description: See your calendars and events. Nothing can be changed.

access.label: Read and write
access.description: Also create, update, delete and answer events.

entries.name: Gmail
entries.tagline: Search and read your mail, and write drafts when you allow it
entries.about: Searches threads, reads messages and drafts, lists labels, and (at the Read and organize level) writes drafts, labels, trashes and marks spam. It cannot send mail. Gmail's read scopes are restricted by Google, which matters for a public release of Dara.

access.label: Read only
access.description: Search and read mail. Nothing can be changed.

access.label: Read and organize
access.description: Also write drafts, label, trash and mark spam. It cannot send.

entries.name: Canva
entries.tagline: Search, create, autofill and export Canva designs
entries.about: Works with your Canva designs, folders and brand templates. The server registers Dara itself when you sign in, so there is nothing to set up.

entries.name: Firecrawl
entries.tagline: Search the web and pull clean content from any page
entries.about: Searches the web, scrapes a page into clean text, and researches documentation and papers, so Dara can answer from current sources. It can also run longer research jobs. Sign in with your Firecrawl account (single sign-on); the server registers Dara itself, so there is nothing to set up. Pages and searches are sent to Firecrawl.

entries.name: Context7
entries.tagline: Current documentation and code examples for programming libraries
entries.about: Finds a library and returns its up-to-date documentation and examples, so Dara answers coding questions from the current docs instead of from memory. There is no sign-in and nothing to set up. The library names and questions Dara sends are visible to Context7.

entries.name: DeepWiki
entries.tagline: Documentation and answers about public GitHub repositories
entries.about: Reads the generated wiki of a public GitHub repository, lists its pages, and answers questions about how the code works. There is no sign-in and nothing to set up. Only public repositories are covered, and the repository names and questions Dara sends are visible to DeepWiki.

entries.name: Hugging Face
entries.tagline: Search public models, datasets and Spaces on the Hugging Face Hub
entries.about: Searches the Hub for models, datasets and Spaces, shows the details of a repository, and browses its files. Without signing in it sees public data only. There is nothing to set up.

entries.name: Todoist
entries.tagline: Look at your tasks and projects, and manage them when you allow it
entries.about: Lets Dara read your Todoist tasks and projects and, when you allow it, add and change them. Sign in with your Todoist account; the server registers Dara itself, so there is nothing to set up. Dara asks before using any tool unless you allow it.

entries.name: Tavily
entries.tagline: Search the web and read pages for current answers
entries.about: Searches the web and pulls the content of pages, so Dara can answer from current sources. Sign in with your Tavily account; the server registers Dara itself, so there is nothing to set up. Searches and page addresses are sent to Tavily.

entries.name: Airtable
entries.tagline: Work with the records in your Airtable bases
entries.about: Lets Dara look at your Airtable bases and tables and, when you allow it, change records. Sign in with your Airtable account and choose which bases to share; the server registers Dara itself, so there is nothing to set up. Dara asks before using any tool unless you allow it.

entries.name: Outlook mail and calendar
entries.tagline: Your Outlook mail and calendar through Microsoft Graph
entries.about: Microsoft does not offer a hosted MCP server for Outlook that Dara can rely on, so this will be a built-in connector that reads through Microsoft Graph with read-only permissions. Not available yet.
